categories.main_business_segments: NAGAILEBEN operates a single business segment focused on the planning, manufacturing, and sales of medical wear, including uniforms for healthcare and nursing professionals, as well as related products such as shoes. The company and its consolidated subsidiary, NAGAI Hakui Kogyo, are engaged in the end-to-end value chain from product planning to delivery, with the core business being medical and healthcare apparel.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary apparel CAD/CAM systems for design and automated cutting, enabling efficient and high-quality production. It emphasizes the development of high-function, high-sensitivity, and high-quality materials, often through joint development with textile manufacturers. Production is carried out both domestically and overseas, with a focus on multi-variety, small-lot manufacturing and rapid delivery. The company also develops functional textiles (e.g., antimicrobial, antistatic, stretch, and easy-care) and sustainable products such as reusable surgical gowns.
categories.primary_customers_markets: NAGAILEBEN's primary customers are medical and nursing care institutions, including hospitals, clinics, and care facilities. The core market consists of healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, caregivers), while peripheral markets include patients (patient wear) and surgical environments (surgical wear). The company also serves major distributors, with one key customer, WATANUKYU SEIMOA, accounting for about 19% of sales.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s main market is Japan, which accounts for over 90% of sales and assets. It also has a growing presence in East Asia, particularly Taiwan and South Korea, with direct sales offices established in these regions. Overseas production is conducted in Southeast Asia to optimize costs and supply chain resilience.
categories.supply_chain_position: NAGAILEBEN operates primarily in the downstream segment of the supply chain, focusing on the planning, manufacturing, and sales of finished medical apparel and related products. It sources materials from textile manufacturers and outsources some production to overseas factories, but controls product planning, design, and final sales to end customers and distributors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include deepening its core healthcare and doctor wear markets with high-end and high-value-added products, expanding share in peripheral markets (surgical and patient wear), and developing overseas business in East Asia. R&D focuses on functional and sustainable materials, infection control products, and environmentally friendly solutions (e.g., reusable surgical packs). There is also an emphasis on rapid response to market trends, digitalization, and strengthening the integrated planning-production-sales model.
categories.revenue_model: NAGAILEBEN generates revenue primarily through the sale of physical products—medical uniforms, patient wear, surgical wear, and shoes—to healthcare institutions and distributors. Revenue is recognized upon delivery or shipment of goods, with some products sold under licensing agreements for branded items.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company is a leading player in the Japanese medical apparel market, known for its high market share and strong brand recognition. Key competitors include other domestic medical uniform manufacturers and global brands entering the Japanese market. NAGAILEBEN differentiates itself through its integrated value chain, product quality, and focus on functional and sustainable innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending August 2025, consolidated net sales were approximately 17.0 billion yen, with operating profit of 3.6 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 2.6 billion yen. The company has a high equity ratio (over 90%), stable cash flow, and a conservative financial structure. While recent years have seen slight revenue declines due to market headwinds, the company is targeting renewed growth, aiming for 18.0 billion yen in sales in FY2026 and 19.5 billion yen by FY2028.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: NAGAILEBEN emphasizes high-quality, functional, and comfortable medical wear that supports healthcare professionals’ performance and well-being. Its products are differentiated by advanced textile technologies (antimicrobial, stretch, easy-care), design aesthetics, and sustainability (reusable, long-life products). The company also highlights its ability to deliver a wide variety of products in small lots with short lead times, and its commitment to supporting the healthcare sector through continuous innovation and customer-centric product development.
